who: Sushruta Samhita, Chikitsa XXIV · tr. K. K. L. Bhishagratna, 1911
quote: Diseases fly from the presence of a person, habituated to regular physical exercise... just as small beasts do on seeing a lion.
meaning: An old Indian medical book says: sickness runs from people who exercise, like small animals from a lion.

who: Hua Tuo, physician, about 200 CE · Sanguozhi, tr. Victor H. Mair, 1994
quote: The human body needs exertion... but it shouldn't be pushed to the limit. Movement of the limbs... enables the blood in the arteries to flow freely, preventing sickness from occurring. It's like a door-pivot that never decays...
meaning: Your body needs to move, but not until you are worn out. Moving keeps the blood flowing.

who: Hippocratic writings · Regimen I.2, tr. W. H. S. Jones, 1931
quote: ...eating alone will not keep a man well; he must also take exercise. For food and exercise, while possessing opposite qualities, yet work together to produce health.
meaning: Good food alone cannot keep you healthy. You also need to move.

who: Charaka Samhita, Sutrasthana 7.32 · tr. Jamnagar edition, 1949
quote: Lightness, capacity for work, firmness, tolerance to hardship... and stimulation of the gastric fire accrue from exercise.
meaning: The old Ayurveda books say exercise makes you light, steady and strong, and helps you digest.

who: Suwen (Basic Questions), Chinese medical classic, ch. 2 · tr. from Chinese
quote: ...the sage does not treat illness that has already come, but treats it before it comes... it is like digging a well when you are already thirsty... Is that not too late?
meaning: Look after your health before you get sick. Don't wait until you're thirsty to dig the well.

who: The Buddha · Anguttara Nikaya 5.29, tr. Bhikkhu Sujato, 2018
quote: ...there are five benefits of walking meditation... You get fit for traveling, fit for striving in meditation, and healthy. What's eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is properly digested...
meaning: The Buddha said walking practice keeps you fit and well, and helps you digest food.

who: Plutarch · Advice about Keeping Well 24, tr. F. C. Babbitt, 1928
quote: ...health is not to be purchased by idleness and inactivity... the man who thinks to conserve his health by uselessness and ease does not differ from him who guards his eyes by not seeing, and his voice by not speaking.
meaning: Sitting still won't save your health. That's like saving your eyes by never looking.

who: Wat Pho hermit statues, Bangkok, 1830s · K. I. Matics, Journal of the Siam Society, 1977
quote: At Wat Pho in Bangkok, statues of hermits made in the 1830s show ‘ruesi dat ton’, Thai self-stretching exercises. Each figure was meant to ease a problem, such as stiff legs, sprained shoulders or dizziness.
meaning: Thailand has its own old stretching practice for aches and stiffness.

who: Chinese folk saying · Thomas Fuller, Gnomologia no. 6251, 1732
quote: A Chinese folk saying goes: ‘Walk a hundred steps after a meal, and live to ninety-nine.’ An English proverb book of 1732 says: ‘After Dinner, sit a while: After Supper, walk a Mile.’
meaning: Two countries, same advice: after you eat, take a gentle walk.

who: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Life, 2005
quote: Physical health is not a commodity to be bargained for... it has to be earned through sweat. It is something that we must build up.
meaning: You cannot buy good health. You build it yourself, with effort and sweat.
